hypotheses.reasoning: At 22:25:11 auth-svc reloaded IDP_API_KEY from the secrets store (version 24) and version 23 was revoked (#202). Logins were succeeding right up to that point (#205, #211). From 22:25:51 on, every call auth-svc makes to the identity provider is rejected with 401 invalid API key (#217, #226, #232, #242). auth-svc passes this back as a 502, account-svc logs AuthClient.issueToken failures (#218), and edge-proxy returns 502s on POST /login. The key rotation is the cause: the new key is not valid at the IdP, or it was never registered there, and the old one is already revoked. Things I ruled out: the single connection reset at 22:19 (#114) recovered on retry; the slow audit_log query (#216) and the 429 throttle (#195) have nothing to do with the login path; the IdP is up, since it answers quickly with 401s and is not timing out or returning 5xx.
The IdP could be having a problem of its own with key validation. Against that: the 401s start right after our own key rotation, and the only other IdP error was one transient reset earlier.

verdict.recommendedAction: Roll auth-svc back to IDP_API_KEY version 23 by un-revoking it, or register or fix version 24 with the identity provider, then reload the secrets in auth-svc. Check that POST /tokens works again. After that, put the rotation process behind a check that confirms the new key works before the old one is revoked.
